args.name: stop-jobs
args.description: Consent to stop file operations that are running: they are told to start nothing further, the one in progress is finished, and the program closes. Without it, quit is refused (busy) while file operations run.

exitCodes.meaning: busy: file operations are running and --stop-jobs was not given, or a window is open

examples.expect: 0, and no viewer process is left

commands.name: open
commands.summary: Show a file or a folder in the viewer, or hand a resource locator or a document the viewer reads to the dialog that reads it. The bare launch (the verb word left out) is this verb.

args.name: target
args.description: A file, a folder, an archive, a UNC share path, a resource locator (sftp:// or gd://), a Share Manager document (.fmscfg, .fmsexch while the exchange client is offered) or a live broadcast descriptor (a .fmsbcast file or an intent link). An internal ::name:: token is refused. An address may carry a user name and password (smb://user:password@host/share): the value is never written to the log or an answer.

args.name: target-file
args.description: Read the target from this file instead of the command line (one line, UTF-8), so an address with a password stays out of the shell history. Give either the target or this option.

args.name: no-back
args.description: Keep background tasks off for the session (the shipped -NoBack switch, any letter case, before or after the target).

args.name: json
args.description: print the response line instead of a sentence

args.name: result
args.description: write the returned data to this file, whole

returns.name: kind
returns.description: what the target turned out to be: image, video, audio, document, archive, folder, resource or other

returns.name: count
returns.description: how many files the folder listing holds; no names

exitCodes.meaning: shown, or handed to the dialog that reads it
not proven: the running program may still be working
no target given, both a target and --target-file given, or the file holds no single line
the target or the --target-file file does not exist, or the viewer is busy
the network share did not answer

examples.expect: exit 0; the folder is on screen
exit 0; the file holds {"kind":"video","count":N}
exit 0; the address in the file is open, and it is in neither the shell history nor the log

commands.name: phone-code receive
commands.summary: Take the connection code a phone showed (relayed by the Share Manager) into the Resources panel's import dialog; nothing is added until the person confirms.

args.name: secret-file
args.description: A UTF-8 file that holds the phone connection code, or the code document the Share Manager opened. The viewer reads it, keeps nothing and never logs it. The shipped ::fms-phone-code:: spelling carries the code itself inside the window message, never on a command line.

exitCodes.meaning: the file does not exist, or the viewer is busy
the setting that lets other programs ask this app to work with files, screen, clipboard or the network is off

examples.expect: exit 0; the import dialog shows what would be added

commands.name: stream-catalog build
commands.summary: Build a stream-catalog.zip from an M3U or M3U8 playlist or a folder of playlists.

args.name: input
args.description: The playlist file or the folder that holds playlists.

args.name: out
args.description: The archive to write; stream-catalog.zip in the input folder (or beside the input file) when absent. The shipped option spellings -o, /o, --output and /output are accepted after a shipped verb spelling.

args.name: overwrite
args.description: Replace an existing archive, under the churn guard. The shipped verb spellings imply it, because they always replaced.

args.name: force
args.description: Bypass the churn guard that refuses a replacement losing more than 20 percent of the previous identities. The shipped spellings -f, /f, --force and /force are accepted.

args.name: json
args.description: print the response line instead of a sentence

args.name: result
args.description: write the returned data to this file, whole

returns.name: rows
returns.description: rows written

returns.name: passed
returns.description: whether the built archive passed its own checks

exitCodes.meaning: the build failed or the churn guard refused
the setting that lets other programs ask this app to work with files, screen, clipboard or the network is off

examples.expect: exit 0; the archive exists
